name: Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction

criteria.description: Recurrent or chronic signs and symptoms of intestinal obstruction (distension, pain, nausea/vomiting, constipation)
Radiographic evidence of dilated bowel with air-fluid levels during episodes
Absence of mechanical obstruction (confirmed by comprehensive imaging and/or laparotomy)
Abnormal GI motility testing (manometry showing neuropathic or myopathic patterns)
Involvement of other hollow viscera (urinary bladder dysfunction, esophageal dysmotility)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Chronic or recurrent symptoms of intestinal obstruction with radiographic evidence of dilated bowel in the absence of any mechanical cause. Duration typically > 6 months.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classified as neuropathic (enteric nervous system dysfunction) or myopathic (smooth muscle dysfunction). May be primary (idiopathic/genetic) or secondary (autoimmune, paraneoplastic, metabolic, drug-induced).

laboratory: Nutritional deficiencies (iron, B12, folate, fat-soluble vitamins)
Glucose hydrogen breath test positive for SIBO
imaging: Abdominal X-ray: dilated small bowel loops with air-fluid levels during episodes
CT abdomen: dilated bowel without mechanical transition point, possible pneumatosis
Upper GI/small bowel follow-through: dilated loops with delayed transit
genetic: ACTG2 gene mutations (visceral myopathy; autosomal dominant)
MYH11 gene mutations (smooth muscle myosin heavy chain)
other: Antroduodenal manometry: neuropathic pattern (uncoordinated contractions) or myopathic pattern (low-amplitude contractions)
Full-thickness intestinal biopsy: definitive for classification (neuropathic vs myopathic)
Wireless motility capsule to assess regional transit

distinguishingFeatures: Acute pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie) is a single/acute episode in hospitalized patients
Acute form has identifiable precipitant and resolves
Gastroparesis is limited to gastric dysmotility
Normal small bowel transit in gastroparesis
Mechanical obstruction has identifiable transition point on imaging
Surgical adhesions, tumors, or hernias causing obstruction

redFlags: New-onset pseudo-obstruction in adult > 40 years (screen for paraneoplastic cause/occult malignancy)
Signs of bowel ischemia or perforation during pseudo-obstruction episode
Central or peripheral neuropathy with GI dysmotility (consider MNGIE)
references: Antonucci A, et al. Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction. World J Gastroenterol. 2008;14(19):2953-2961.
Di Nardo G, et al. Review article: molecular, pathological and therapeutic features of human enteric neuropathies. Aliment Pharmacol Ther. 2008;28(1):25-42.
Iida H, et al. Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Clin Gastroenterol. 2023;57(3):243-252.
